text:
maya: Quick heads-up — ran an architecture sweep for INT4/INT8/FP8 across sm90/sm92/sm95 with seqlen buckets [64,256,1024,2048]. Found a regression in the FP8 long-sequence (>1024) path when batch size is small. Details + repro below.

alex: Can you paste the profile/output you saw? :eyes:

maya: Paste from the perf run: 
```
profile: model=redwood-v1
batch=1
seq=2048
arch=sm92
quant=fp8
kernel_pick: fp8_attention_fused_v2
latency_ms=142.3  # baseline for this config was ~120.1
kv_warmup_ms=30.1
memcopy_ms=12.4
kernel_exec_ms=98.7
other_overhead_ms=1.1
```

priya: Oof, 30ms warmup is big for a single request. Did we change KV chunking or workspace behavior for FP8?

maya: Yes — the recent per-arch profile flip enabled aggressive KV chunking + workspace coalescing for fp8 on sm92 to optimize throughput. That changed warp scheduling a bit and increased divergence in the attention kernel for long sequences. We also enabled quant_post_scale_bias=true in the fp8 profile.

jamal: Repro steps so I can run locally?

maya: Repro commands: 
```
# repro locally
./tools/run_bench --model redwood-v1 --arch sm92 --quant fp8 --batch 1 --seq 2048 --out profile_sm92_fp8_2048.json
# runtime request example
curl -X POST $RUNTIME/api/v1/infer -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"redwood-v1","quant":"fp8","batch":1,"seq":2048}'
```

alex: Quick mitigation idea: add a seqlen-based hysteresis so the kernel picker doesn't switch to the longpath unless seq > threshold for fp8. Also consider per-arch hysteresis window to avoid flip-flopping under bursty traffic. e.g. 
```
kernel_picker.seqlen_thresholds = "int4:512,int8:768,fp8:1536"
kernel_picker.per_arch_hysteresis_ms = 10
```

priya: Also try disabling the aggressive KV chunking for fp8 on sm92 as an A/B to validate. If warmup drops, we know chunking is the culprit.

maya: I ran a quick patch: set seqlen_threshold for fp8 to 1536 and per_arch_hysteresis_ms=12, and reverted kv_chunking to conservative for sm92. New numbers: 
```
latency_ms=125.6
kv_warmup_ms=12.3
kernel_exec_ms=99.0
memcopy_ms=11.8
```
So overall improved from 142.3 -> 125.6 on that scenario. Still slightly above baseline but much better.

deploy-bot: Rolling out canary with patch branch=fix/quant-hysteresis to cluster c-canary-3 (50% traffic) :rocket:

jamal: Observation for infra: current traces don't surface kernel_id or quant_profile. We need those emitted as tags so dashboards can show which kernel was picked per request.

maya: Filed PR to emit kernel_id and quant_profile as request-level tags (https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4287). Added a short-term logging flag for canary.

alex: Nice. Once canary stabilizes, let's schedule a sweep for sm90/95 with the same knobs and collect 99th percentile numbers. Add an automated test in pickbench to cover seq=1024/2048 for fp8.

priya: Also add a metric for kv_warmup_ms in the console so Optimize can recommend profile changes automatically.

maya: Yep — added a ticket under ENG-RUNTIME-1294 to add kv_warmup_ms and kernel_id tags to the telemetry pipeline.

alex: ack. Priority next sprint. Thanks for the quick triage :thumbsup:

maya: Will follow up with links to canary dashboards and full profile artifacts once the canary has run for an hour.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout succeeded on 50% traffic, no error rate change observed after 15m.

jamal: Great. After we merge, let's also add an automated daily job that runs the seqlen/quant sweep and flags regressions >5% compared to baseline.

maya: Agreed — adding that to ENG-RUNTIME-1294 as an acceptance criteria.

alex: Cool. End of thread for now.
